, and cache discounts are all counted per request, which is why an innocuous-looking question can cost a surprising amount: the cost isn't proportional to your message, it's proportional to the number of requests times the size of the context each one carries.

. A turn is one exchange with you, and a single turn — "fix the failing test" — plays out as a chain of requests:
Runs them, appends the failure output
Tool call: read the test file
Tool call: read the source file
Tool call: edit the source file
Applies the edit, appends the result
Tool call: run the tests again
Runs them, appends the pass output
Six requests for one turn — each one re-sending the whole context. When you wonder where the
went, count the requests, not the turns.
